To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 2D modeling approach is not appropriate for the assessment of seismic fragility of industrial steel buildings, and (ii) residual drifts must be considered in the assessment of seismic risk of all structures.

(i) the modeling of roof truss out-of-plane joint displacement is of utmost importance to properly capture the failure mode of instability of a portion of truss, and (ii) residual drifts, as well as peak transient values, should be considered in the evaluation of probability of failure, especially for structures that are relatively stiff but weak.
